newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Robeco Group sees substantial growth, takeovers.
newsitem.headline: Robeco Group sees substantial growth, takeovers.

text.p: The Robeco group of investment funds said on Wednesday it expected substantial growth in the coming years and was planning to buy asset management firms outside the Netherlands.
Chairman Piet Korteweg said the group was aiming for assets under management of about 150 billion guilders by the end of the year 2001, compared with 87 billion now.
"For that we need both strong investment results and strong distribution channels," he told a news conference. He added that growth of this size could not be realised in the Netherlands alone.
The group is looking for well-positioned asset management firms in the United States and Europe that can be taken over with their client base.

Last year, Robeco bought Argyll Property Asset Managers in Britain. Earlier this month, it took a first step towards international growth by taking a 40 percent stake in U.S. asset management firm Smith Graham & Co.

Korteweg said the capital injection from Rabobank Nederland, which recently took over 50 percent of the Robeco group's management vehicle and will later buy the other half, was used to finance the international expansion.
The Robeco group has split up its marketing activities into a unit which targets institutional investors and one which will be aimed at private clients.
The banking outlets of Rabobank in the Netherlands will be used much more than previously to address private investors and offer them Robeco's products.
Korteweg said the group would also launch various new investment products in the years ahead.
